doc.title: Avakian George — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Yale, Stearns and the big bands
title: Not saving papers and letters
summary: He regrets discarding letters from Armstrong and daily calendars.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: No, I didn’t. I wish I had. In fact, when I left – well, all through my working life, I didn’t keep my daily calendars and all that. I used to, but it just piled up. I had so much paper. And of course I don’t want to put the onus on my wife, but she was right. “Don’t save so much, because it’s getting out of hand.” You see? Having spent over 50 years in the music business, you could imagine. This room could have been filled with papers, and I mean filled. You wouldn’t be able to walk through the room. You’d be walking on top of papers. Anyway, I have a certain amount, but not nearly as much as I wish I had.
Not many. It’s terrible. I threw away letters from people like Louis Armstrong.
I was going to say, his letters are famous.
He was a great letter writer.

He was. When I say threw away, I guess it just kind of got lost in the shuffle over the years. But I have a few. Where they are, I don’t know. That’s why the basement is a mess. I have boxes that I haven’t opened in – sometimes . . .
